images.title: Diagonal splits a corner
images.purpose: Show that in a rectangle that is not a square, a diagonal splits a corner into two unequal angles that add up to 90 degrees.
images.composition: One large rectangle centred, with one angle pair shown at the bottom left corner.
images.exact_structure: One rectangle PQRS, 6 cm long and 4 cm wide, corners P bottom left, Q bottom right, R top right, S top left. One diagonal PR in grey #6B7280. At P the two angles are shaded: the lower angle (between PQ and PR) teal #0072B2 and about 34 degrees, the upper angle (between PR and PS) amber #E69F00 and about 56 degrees, the teal one clearly smaller. Exactly 1 rectangle, 1 diagonal, 2 shaded angles.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
two equal angles at the corner
images.takeaway: The two angles add up to 90 degrees but are not equal.
images.description: A 6 cm by 4 cm rectangle with diagonal PR; at P the small angle of about 34 degrees in teal and the larger angle of about 56 degrees in amber.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the two angles at P, say which is bigger, then read the sum.

image_decisions.why: One corner, two angles and their sum is the whole idea.
